Hungary’s lakes and rivers hit record lows as severe drought deepens Copy/paste the link below: Copy Copy/paste the article video embed link below: Copy Updated: 21/08/2026 - 12:54 GMT+2 Hungary is facing a severe water crisis, with prolonged heat and drought driving water levels sharply lower. Around 99% of the country is under severe or extreme drought, while desertification threatens the Great Hungarian Plain. … More At Lake Velence , Hungary’s third-largest lake, the water level at Agárd fell to around 20 centimetres on 16 August . That is far below the roughly 150 centimetres considered optimal for August and well below the previous record low of 53 centimetres, recorded during the 2022 drought. ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT The shallow, warm water has forced swimming beaches to close and made boating increasingly difficult. Dead fish have appeared along the shore, while large sections of the lakebed are exposed, cracked and dry. The smaller Lake Garancsi , north-west of Budapest, is also close to disappearing. Once popular for fishing, swimming and ice skating, and known as a filming location for the Hungarian comedy Üvegtigris ( Glass Tiger ), it now consists largely of shallow pools surrounded by exposed lakebed. Its water level has fallen by about a centimetre a day during the hottest periods. The Danube has also reached record lows in Budapest , exposing sandbanks and parts of the riverbed beneath the city’s bridges and making navigation more difficult. The low water is also putting pressure on Hungary’s energy system. At the Paks nuclear power plant , which relies on the Danube for cooling and generates nearly half of the country’s electricity, output fell to around 25% of capacity. Engineers have taken measures to maintain sufficient cooling water and prevent a shutdown. Climate change is intensifying heat and contributing to longer dry periods, but experts say Hungary’s water-management system has also made the country more vulnerable. For decades, drainage networks have been designed to remove water from agricultural land and wetlands rather than retain it. Hungary now has more than 40,000 kilometres of drainage canals , while a 2023 study estimated that more than 80% of the country’s historical wetlands had been lost. Environmental groups are calling for a shift towards retaining water in the landscape by restoring wetlands, repairing water-control infrastructure and allowing floodplains to absorb more water. Authorities have begun directing water towards vulnerable wetlands, including the Hortobágy marshes, but environmental groups say much broader changes will be needed to protect Hungary’s remaining lakes, rivers and wetlands from increasingly severe droughts. https://enrsi.stvr.sk/articles/topical-i.text: Prime Minister Robert Fico (Smer-SD) did not travel to Ukraine for the "Carpathian Eight" summit on Friday. The Government Office confirmed that he was unable to attend due to health issues. He was represented by Deputy Foreign Minister Marek Eštok. Roman Michelko, chairman of the coalition SNS parliamentary group, responded: “Mr. Eštok is a so-called "sherpa"; he attends all European Union summits, and I prepare background materials for him. There is no doubt that he is a highly qualified diplomat.” Representatives from the Czech Republic, Ukraine, Romania, Serbia, Poland, Austria, and Hungary met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and the new Ukrainian Prime Minister, Serhiy Koretskyi. Fuel prices were also part of the discussion. During his visit to Prešov on Thursday (17 September), Fico expressed concerns about how the conflict in Ukraine is developing, saying that the situation had never been as serious and tense in terms of the possibility of a pan-European military conflict as it is now. „I do not want Slovakia to become part of any armed conflict simply because of Article 5. Yes, we are in NATO and we value that, but as Prime Minister, I will do everything in my power to ensure that Slovakia is never dragged into an armed conflict,” stated Fico. According to Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty, an armed attack against one NATO member is considered to be an attack against all members. It therefore assumes that member states will come to the aid of the member under attack. The Czech president Petr Pavel said on Sunday that he considers Fico's statement about Article 5 as serious. "If someone says that they are glad to be a member of NATO, in other words, that NATO protects us, but at the same time they are unwilling to get involved if anyone else comes under attack, then they have misunderstood what solidarity means," said Pavel. I respect that Czech President Petr Pavel, as a former NATO general, would like to fight; therefore, I would welcome it if he respected that I prefer peace, Fico said in response. In a speech delivered at the ceremonial swearing-in of military cadets on Saturday, President Peter Pellegrini emphasized that Slovakia should be an active member of NATO. He stated that the country neither desires nor intends to be a passive member of the North Atlantic Alliance, but rather an active and full contributor to the collective security system. The opposition views this as a challenge directed at the Prime Minister, whereas the coalition maintains that this approach simply advocates for peaceful solutions. Source: STVR

REUTERS/Callaghan O'Hare 'My God': Karoline Leavitt shamed after major math goof blows up 'lunatic' attack By: Alexander Willis Sep 29, 2026 6:53AM ET Alexander Willis Alexander Willis is a senior editor who graduated from the Mayborn School of Journalism at the University of North Texas and currently lives in the Metro Nashville area, Tennessee. Prior to joining Raw Story, he covered the Alabama Legislature and governor’s office for Alabama Daily News, and before that, covered government and politics for the Williamson Scene in Middle Tennessee. SEE FULL BIO Make us preferred on Google Comments 0 Share Article Former White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt took to Fox News Monday night to accuse Democratic candidates of flip-flopping on their policy positions, but critics quickly noted that her questionable math appeared to undercut her own argument. “The Democrats are always incredibly disingenuous,” Leavitt said while appearing on Hannity. “They campaign as moderates, they do 360s on every single policy position they have to try to appeal to common sense, good-hearted Americans, but then, when they are elected, they govern as complete radical extreme liberal lunatics.” As noted by countless critics, Leavitt’s accusation that Democratic candidates “do 360s” on their policy positions was a mathematical misfire, as to do a 360 would mean ending up where one started. The phrase Leavitt was likely reaching for, critics said, was “ doing a 180 ,” which means to reverse one’s position. “Former math teacher here. Oh my god,” wrote Hemant Mehta , a podcast host, author and television personality, in a social media post on X. Progressive political commentator Alex Cole, founder of the independent progressive news and analysis website acnewsitics , called Leavitt a “damn idiot,” and reminded Leavitt that “a 360 brings you back to the same position.” “This unintentional self-own kills me!” wrote South Dakota attorney and public prosecutor Craig Evenson . And Czech journalist Vojtěch Gibiš sarcastically quipped that Leavitt’s jab at Democratic candidates exposed her “mathematical talent.” “The USA had already laughed at her statements about reducing drug prices by ‘200 or 300%’ or her claim that she spends ‘95% of her time working, which gives her only 25% of time for childcare’ and now she claims about Democrats that after being elected they do a 360-degree [pivot],” Gibiš wrote in a social media post on X, according to an automatic translation from X’s Grok chatbot. Ukraine unveils flying ambulance drone that could save lives in minutes Copy/paste the link below: Copy Copy/paste the article video embed link below: Copy Updated: 16/10/2026 - 10:41 GMT+2 A Ukrainian company has demonstrated an unusual new battlefield rescue system: a drone capable of carrying a wounded soldier inside an enclosed cabin. Developed by SkyFall, the aircraft, named StarGate, was filmed taking off, flying and landing with a person on board. … More Built to reach casualties in areas inaccessible to ground vehicles, the remotely operated machine can reportedly lift 150 kg and travel at speeds of up to 105 km/h . Its ability to fly over minefields , rivers and damaged roads could help shorten dangerous journeys from the front line. ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT In the footage, a SkyFall representative steps out of the cabin after landing, while an operator remains at a distance. The manufacturer says StarGate could cut evacuation times from hours or days to just minutes , potentially allowing wounded troops to receive medical attention much sooner. The aircraft uses Starlink and SkyFall's L-Link system, together with AI-assisted technology designed to operate despite satellite navigation interference. It was also shown deploying a net to intercept a hostile drone . A Ukrainian combat brigade has now received the prototype for testing under frontline conditions. SkyFall has yet to publish the findings, and the drone's performance in real combat evacuations remains to be independently confirmed . https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ck5y.text: Image source, Andrej ISAKOVIC / AFP via Getty Images Image caption, Officers were visible outside the embassy in Belgrade later on Wednesday By Vicky Wong Published 1 hour ago Serbian police shot dead a young man outside the Israeli embassy in Belgrade in the early hours of Wednesday after what authorities called a "terrorist attack". The country's interior minister, Ivica Dacic, said the attacker had rushed at a police officer with two knives while shouting the phrase "Allahu Akbar". The officer sustained a minor knife wound to the face and shot the attacker. Dacic said the suspect has not been identified, but he was a minor and Serbian citizen who was being monitored by security services as he was "known to be a supporter of the Islamic State". Speaking to reporters outside the embassy, Dacic said an investigation is ongoing, but security services said the suspect had posted a picture of the Islamic State flag on his Instagram. Dacic raised the country's terrorism threat level to "red alert" - the highest threat level â meaning stricter security checks and increased police presence at places like infrastructure facilities and areas where large crowds gather. The interior minister said he had visited the injured police officer, who was reportedly doing well and did not need hospital care for his wounds. Armed security personnel were seen standing guard outside the Israeli embassy on Wednesday morning. Israel's foreign ministry confirmed in a social media post that no embassy personnel were injured and the mission was closed at the time of the incident. This is the second such attack on Belgrade's Israeli embassy in less than three years; in June 2024, a man shot a police officer in the neck with a crossbow. The officer who was shot survived the attack and shot dead the assailant, identified as a Serbian man who had converted to Islam. Wednesday's attack comes just one day after elections in Israel.
